_what: HERO per-page copy (design doc §4.2 rows 6-10): the badge's problem clause and its attribution tail, the H1, the answer capsule body and its possessive close, and the value panel's head strong + claim + 5 generic-vs-ours rows + foot sentence.
badge_tail: Written by people who have been in a hot house
answer_body_html: Check 4 things: thermostat mode and fan setting, the filter, whether the outdoor unit is running, and ice on the copper line. Ice means switch cooling off and leave the fan on first. If those look normal, it is something you cannot confirm by eye: an outdoor electrical or start issue, a coil or airflow problem, or refrigerant. Those need measurements at the equipment.
cap_last_html: Start with what your AC is actually doing.
vp_head_strong: This is not another AC troubleshooting article.
vp_claim_pos: Articles list every possible cause. We use our tool to walk your actual system LIVE.

value_rows.generic: An article lists eight causes for no particular house.
value_rows.ours_html: We rule causes out using your thermostat reading and your filter.

value_rows.generic: A video is somebody else's unit, filmed once, in good light.
value_rows.ours_html: We look at yours, in whatever state it is in at 9pm tonight.

value_rows.generic: A forum reply says just swap the capacitor.
value_rows.ours_html: We tell you which parts hold a charge after the power is off, so you don't fry yourself.

value_rows.generic: An AI summary cannot see your equipment.
value_rows.ours_html: We read your model from a photo and narrow it from there.

value_rows.generic: Calling around means explaining it four times.
value_rows.ours_html: You leave with a packet that arrives before the technician does.

vp_foot_html: Two houses with the same symptom often need different next steps. We build from your equipment, your observations and what you have already ruled out, not from an average of everyone else's AC.
